IR.rationale: A rising 5Y-FedFunds spread signals a hawkish repricing of the expected US policy path. That tightens global discount rates and dollar funding, which weighs on foreign equity returns.

B.rationale: Strong USD EM sovereign bond returns mark easy global dollar credit and rising risk appetite. These conditions tend to carry over into non-US equity returns.

V.rationale: When implied volatility and policy uncertainty are jointly elevated, investors demand a higher risk premium. Subsequent returns are therefore higher on average (the variance-risk-premium and uncertainty-premium mechanism).

AP.rationale: Strong recent US market returns tend to partially reverse at short horizons. They also co-move with already-priced global news, so their sign for future returns carries information.

ST.rationale: Strong momentum payoffs indicate trending, risk-on markets that are prone to later unwinds. This captures crowding in global equity positioning.

FX.rationale: Broad dollar strength tightens global financial conditions and lowers dollar-translated returns on foreign equities.

COM.rationale: Rising oil prices signal strong global demand, which supports cyclical European and Asian earnings.

MC.rationale: Tight financial conditions restrict leverage and risk-taking and predict weaker subsequent equity returns.

ENDG.rationale: The index's own recent strength captures short-horizon momentum or reversal in its returns.

IR.rationale: Falling medium-term yields relative to policy rates reflect flight to safety and growth scares. Such episodes precede higher equity volatility.

B.rationale: Widening Baa spreads together with weak high-yield returns mark credit deterioration. Credit stress leads equity volatility through the leverage and funding channels.

V.rationale: Elevated implied volatility in both equities and gold signals broad cross-asset uncertainty. This forecasts realised variance beyond what its own lags already capture.

AP.rationale: A joint sell-off in US and EM equities triggers the leverage effect and global contagion. Both raise subsequent volatility in developed foreign markets.

ST.rationale: Outperformance of profitable firms reflects flight to quality, which accompanies turbulent markets.

FX.rationale: Broad dollar strength together with yen appreciation is the classic risk-off funding-currency move. It precedes higher equity volatility.

COM.rationale: Falling broad commodity prices signal weakening global demand and stress for resource-linked markets, raising volatility.

MC.rationale: Tight financial conditions amplify shocks through constrained intermediaries and raise future variance.

ENDG.rationale: High recent realised variance tends to mean-revert faster than a simple persistence model implies. Its level therefore helps predict the residual.

IR.rationale: Abrupt term-spread steepening reflects term-premium shocks that raise discount rates. These shocks can trigger sharp equity drawdowns.

B.rationale: Deteriorating credit, seen as spread widening with weak high-yield returns, leads equity tail losses because credit markets price default risk early.

V.rationale: Joint elevation of equity and safe-haven implied volatility signals fat left tails across assets.

AP.rationale: Small-cap underperformance reflects tightening liquidity and risk aversion, which precede broad sell-offs.

ST.rationale: Flight to quality within equities signals that investors are de-risking ahead of possible drawdowns.

FX.rationale: Dollar and yen strength together is the risk-off funding-squeeze state, which is associated with crashes in foreign equities.

COM.rationale: Commodity weakness signals deteriorating global growth expectations and raises downside tail risk.

MC.rationale: Tight financial conditions together with high measured stress identify fragile markets in which large losses are more likely.

ENDG.rationale: Weak recent returns indicate a drawdown in progress, and losses cluster in time.

IR.rationale: Falling medium-term rates relative to policy signal expected easing, which can fuel sharp equity rallies.

B.rationale: Strong EM dollar bond returns mark easing global dollar funding and risk appetite, which support large rallies.

V.rationale: High fear and uncertainty raise risk premia and widen the right tail too. Relief rallies follow peaks in uncertainty.

AP.rationale: Recent market weakness sets up short-horizon rebounds through reversal and liquidity provision.

ST.rationale: Momentum losses typically coincide with sharp junk-led rebounds after sell-offs.

FX.rationale: A weakening dollar eases global financial conditions and boosts dollar-measured foreign equity returns.

COM.rationale: Rising oil signals strengthening global demand, which favours strong cyclical upside.

MC.rationale: Elevated financial stress widens both tails. Stressed markets offer large rebound potential once stress abates.

ENDG.rationale: Depressed recent returns raise the chance of a large rebound through mean reversion.
